1.text: Introduction
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 1

1.text: [132] The Letter of Peter, which he dispatched to Philip.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 2

1.text: Peter, the apostle of Jesus Christ, to Philip, our beloved brother, and our co-apostle, as well as the brethren together with you. Greetings.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 3

1.text: I desire for you to understand, our brother, that we received directives from our Lord, the savior of the entire world, for us to assemble together, in order to teach and preach about the salvation promised to us by [133] our Lord Jesus Christ.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 4

1.text: You, however, separated yourself from us, and you desired not to assemble together to learn how we could coordinate ourselves, so that we might announce the message.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 5

1.text: Would it, therefore, be acceptable to you, our brother, to come in accord with the directives of our God, Jesus?
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 6

1.text: When Philip had received and read this, he went to Peter, delighting with glee.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 7

1.text: Peter Gathers the Apostles on the Mount of Olives
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 8

1.text: Peter then assembled the others. They went to the mountain called Olivet, where formerly they would assemble together with the blessed Christ when he dwelt in the body.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 9

1.text: When the apostles were met together, and had fallen to their knees, they prayed as follows, and spoke:
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 10

1.text: “Father, Father, Father of the light,you to whom belong the indestructible ones,listen to us,just as [you] have been delighted in your holy Son, Jesus Christ,because for our sake he has become a light [134] in the darkness.Verily,[1] listen to us.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 11

1.text: And once more they prayed, and spoke:
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 12

1.text: “Son of life, Son of deathlessness,you who dwell in the light,Son, Christ of deathlessness,our redeemer,grant us strength,because they are hunting for us to murder us.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 13

1.text: Jesus Appears to the Apostles
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 14

1.text: A bright light then became visible, and the mountain glowed because of the sight of the one who had become visible, and a voice cried out to them, and said:
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 15

1.text: “Pay attention to my words, so that I can speak to you. Why are you looking for me?I am Jesus Christ, who abides with you continually.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 16

1.text: The apostles responded, and said:
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 17

1.text: “Lord, it would please us to understand the deficiency of the aeons, as well as their fullness,and how we are held back in this dwelling-place.How have we arrived at this place?How will we depart?[135] How do we come to have authority for boldness of speech?Why do the powers battle against us?”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 18

1.text: A voice from the light then cried out to them, and said: “You are the ones who testify that I have spoken all of these things to you, but on account of your unfaithfulness, I will repeat (these things).
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 19

1.text: The Deficiency and the Tyrannical / Proud One
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 20

1.text: “Now, then, regarding [the deficiency] of the aeons, here is the deficiency: When the defiance and thoughtlessness of the Mother became manifest, apart from the order of the Greatness of the Father, she desired to establish aeons. When she spoke, the tyrannical one followed, but when she abandoned a piece, the tyrannical one seized it, and it turned into a deficiency. This is the deficiency of the aeons.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 21

1.text: “When the tyrannical one had taken a piece, he planted it, stationing powers and authorities over it, and he restricted it to inside the mortal aeons. Every cosmic power was gleeful that they had been produced. [136] However, they were ignorant of the pre-existent [Father], given that they are aliens to him. [Instead, this] (tyrannical) one was granted power, and they worshipped him and praised him.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 22

1.text: “Now the mind of the tyrannical one grew arrogant on account of the praise of the powers. He became an opponent and desired to replace an image [with another image] and to replace a form with another form. Now, he delegated the powers under his authority to shape mortal bodies, and they came to exist out of a disparity of the likeness that had been produced.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 23

1.text: The Incarnation
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 24

1.text: “Now, concerning the fullness, it is I, [even] I, who was dispatched down into the body for the sake of this seed that had been lost, and I descended to their mortal mold. They, however, failed to notice me, imagining me to be a mortal person. I spoke with the one who is mine, and he paid attention to me, just like you, too, who have paid attention this day. I granted him authority to come into the inheritance of his fatherhood, and I took [him] [137] [. . .] filled [. . .] by means of his salvation. Given that he was deficiency, he turned into fullness.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 25

1.text: Battling the Powers
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 26

1.text: “However, regarding your detention, it is because you belong to me. When you remove from yourselves what is destructible, then you will become lights among mortals.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 27

1.text: “Regarding your battle against the powers, it results from their lacking rest, unlike yourselves, given that they do not desire for you to be saved.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 28

1.text: Then once more the apostles worshipped, and said: “Lord, instruct us, how shall we battle with the archons, given that the archons are superior to us?”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 29

1.text: A voice then cried out to them from the apparition, and said: “You have to war against them in the following way, because the archons war against the Inner Man. You have to war against them in the following way:
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 30

1.text: “Assemble together and teach salvation accompanied with a promise to the world, and gird yourselves with the power of my Father, and make known your request, and he, the Father, will assist you, as he assisted you when he sent me. [138] [Fear] not, [I will be with you continually], as I spoke to you formerly when I dwelt in the body.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 31

1.text: Then lightning and thunder came from heaven, and the one they had seen in the apparition in that place was snatched to heaven.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 32

1.text: Suffering and Death
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 33

1.text: The apostles then thanked the Lord with all praises and returned to Jerusalem.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 34

1.text: While they were going down (the mountain, heading towards Jerusalem) on the road, they conversed concerning the light that had become visible, and a dispute began concerning the Lord, during which they said: “If he, our Lord, suffered, how much more (will) we?”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 35

1.text: Peter responded, and said: “He suffered for our sake, and we will have to suffer, too, on account of our being small.”[4]
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 36

1.text: A voice then came to them, and said: “I informed you many times that you will have to suffer. You will have to be dragged to synagogues and in front of governors, which will cause you to suffer. He, however, who will not suffer, he, too, [will] not [139] [. . . my] Father [. . .], so that he can [. . .].”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 37

1.text: The aptles, however, were very glad, and went up to Jerusalem, going up to the temple, and teaching salvation in the name of the Lord, Jesus Christ, and they healed [a] multitude.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 38

1.text: Peter, however, began speaking, and said to his disciples: “When our Lord Jesus dwelt in the body, he told us everything, because he himself had descended. My brethren, pay attention to my voice.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 39

1.text: He was filled with a holy Spirit, and spoke in the following way:
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 40

1.text: “Our light, Jesus, [de]scended,and was crucified,and he wore a crown of thorns,and he donned a purple robe,and he was hanged on a tree,and he was interred in a tomb,and he rose from among the dead.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 41

1.text: “My brethren, Jesus is an alien to such suffering as this. We, however, are those who have suffered on account of the trespass of the Mother. This is why he announced everything with a symbolic meaning when he was among us. The Lord Jesus, Son of the measureless glory of the Father, is the author of our life.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 42

1.text: “My brethren, let us pay no attention to these Godless[5] ones, nor walk in [140] [. . .].”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 43

1.text: Conclusion
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 44

1.text: Peter [then] assembled [the others], and said: “[Our Lord], Jesus Christ, author of our repose, grant us a spirit of insight, so that we, too, may be able to work miracles!”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 45

1.text: Peter and the other apostles then saw [him], and they were filled with a holy Spirit, and each one of them performed healings, and they departed to declare the Lord Jesus, and they assembled together, greeted[6] each other, and said: “Amen.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 46

1.text: Jesus then became visible, and said to them: “Peace be with [all] of you, and with all who are faithful in my name. When you leave, however, gladness, grace, and power will be yours.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 47

1.text: “Fear not. Behold, I will be with you continually.”
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 48

1.text: The apostles then departed from each other into four messages[7] to preach, and they went with the power of Jesus, with peace.
1.label: Nag Hammadi Codex VIII · 49

1.text: [1] [Peter, the] apostle of Jesus [Christ], writes to Philip, [my beloved], and my co-apostle, [and] to the brethren. Greetings.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 50

1.text: [Now, I desire] for you to understand, my [brother, that we] received instructions [from] our Lord, even [the savior] of the entire world, [that we would assemble together], in order to [teach and] preach [the] salvation by means of the Lord, [Jesus] Christ.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 51

1.text: You, however, separated yourself [from us], and [you did not . . .] we have [. . .] to preach.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 52

1.text: If, [then], you consider it acceptable, brother, come in accord with the directives of Jesus, our God.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 53

1.text: [. . .] Philip received these, and read these, and he gladly went to Peter.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 54

1.text: Peter then assembled the others. They [then] went up to the Mount of Olives, where they would formerly assemble together with the blessed Christ [2] in the days when he dwelt in the body.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 55

1.text: The apostles then assembled together, and knelt, [and prayed] in the following way:
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 56

1.text: “[Father], Father, Father of the [light],you to whom belong the unpolluted ones, listen to [us! . . .]your [. . .] in [your holy son, Jesus Christ,because] for our sake [he] became a light in the darkness.Verily, listen to us.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 57

1.text: And [they] continued [. . .]:
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 58

1.text: “[. . . deathlessness [. . .][…] listen to us,and grant [us strength], because they are hunting for us to murder us!”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 59

1.text: Then a bright light became visible, so that the mountain glowed from the apparition that had become visible. A voice cried out to them, and said:
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 60

1.text: “Pay attention [to my] words, so that I can speak to you,because you have been looking for me. I am Jesus Christ, who will be with you continually.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 61

1.text: [3] The apostles then responded, and said:
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 62

1.text: “Lord, [the] deficiency of the aeons,as well as their fullness,how do they hold us back [in this dwelling-place,and how] have we arrived at this place,and, how [will we] depart,and how do we come to have the authority for boldness of speech?[Why do the] powers battle against us?”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 63

1.text: [Then] an utterance came out of the light, and said: “You yourselves testify to me that I [. . .] these things [. . .], but on account of your unfaithfulness, I will answer yet again.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 64

1.text: “Now, then, [regarding] the deficiency of the aeons, here is the deficiency, which is defiance. The uninformed Mother became manifest, apart from the order of the Great One. From the beginning, he desired to establish aeons, and when she [spoke], the proud one appeared. Now, a part was abandoned behind her. The proud one seized it, and a deficiency came to exist. Now, this is [4] the deficiency of the aeons.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 65

1.text: “This was because the proud one took the part, and sowed it, and he established [powers] and authorities, [and restricted it] to the [mortal] aeons, [and] every [power] of the world gleeful over their coming to exist. They, however, know not the [Father], who exists from the beginning, [given that] they are aliens to him. Instead, this (proud) one granted them power, and they worshipped and praised him.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 66

1.text: “And the mind of the proud one [grew arrogant on account of] the praise [of the powers], and he [became] an opponent, and they desired to replace an image with another image and (to replace) a form with another form. With his authority, he directed the powers to shape mortal bodies, and something contemptible resulted from the likeness that had arisen.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 67

1.text: “Now concerning the fulfillment, it is I, [even] I, who was dispatched into a body [for the sake of this] seed that had been lost, because it had entered [into a] mortal mold. They, however, failed to notice me. They imagined I was a mortal. I spoke with the one [5] who is mine, and the one who is mine paid attention to me, that is, you are the one [. . .]. [You] are the one who has paid attention [this day], and I granted (you)[2] authority to come into the inheritance of (your)[3] father, [and] I took my own, and the aeons were completed by means of their [salvation. . . .], that is, a reduction]. On account of this, there is also [. . .].
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 68

1.text: “However, regarding your detention, it is because you belong to me. When you remove the flesh from yourselves, then [you will] become lights among mortals.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 69

1.text: “Then you will battle the powers, because they lack rest, unlike you, given that they do not desire for you to be saved.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 70

1.text: Then once more the apostles worshipped, and said: “Son, instruct us, how shall we battle against the archons, given that they, the archons, are (here) below?”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 71

1.text: The voice then cried out from the apparition, [6] and said: “You now, fight in the following way, because the archons battle against the Inner Man. You, however, fight in the following way:
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 72

1.text: “[Assemble] together and teach salvation to the world, and gird yourselves with the power of my Father, and make known your request, and he, the Father, <will assist you, as> he assisted (you) when he sent [me]. Fear [not], I will be with you, as I spoke to you formerly when I dwelt in the body.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 73

1.text: Then a rumbling and thunder came from heaven, and the one they had seen in the apparition [was snatched up] from there.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 74

1.text: The apostles then thanked the Lord with all praises and returned to Jerusalem.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 75

1.text: While they were going along with each other on the road, they conversed with each other concerning the light that had become visible, and [a dispute] began concerning the Lord, during which [they] said: “If he, our [Lord], died, then how much more (will) we ourselves?”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 76

1.text: [7] Peter, however, responded, and said: “He died for our sake. It is appropriate that we ourselves die for the sake of humanity.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 77

1.text: [A voice] then came to them, [and] said: “I’ve told you [many] times that it is appropriate for you [to] die and to be dragged into synagogues and in front of governors. It is appropriate for you [. . .], in which [. . .] disciples [. . .] pray [to] the Father [. . .], so that [he may] defend [you].”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 78

1.text: The apostles, however, were glad [. . .] to Jerusalem, [and they went up to] the temple, [. . .] in the name of Jesus [Christ].
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 79

1.text: “<. . .>. [He] instructed us concerning everything when he dwelt in the body, because he descended.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 80

1.text: Pay attention to my voice, my brethren,” and he was filled with a holy Spirit, and said:
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 81

1.text: “Jesus, our light, came,and was crucified,and he wore a crown of thorns,and he donned a purple robe,and he was hanged on a tree,and he was interred in a tomb,and [8] he rose from among the dead.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 82

1.text: “My brethren, Jesus is alien to death. We, however, have died because of the trespass of our Mother, [and] because of which for our sake he announced everything with a symbolic meaning, given that [the Lord] Jesus is the Son of the measureless glory of the Father. [He is] the author of [our life].
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 83

1.text: “So, my [brethren], let us not pay heed [. . .] nor walk [in the] teaching [. . .].”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 84

1.text: Peter [lifted up] his hands to Heaven, [and said: “Our Lord], Jesus Christ, author [of our] repose, grant us [a spirit] of insight, so that we, too, may be able to work miracles!”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 85

1.text: Peter and the apostles then spoke to Jesus, and they were filled with a holy Spirit, and each one of them performed healings, and they departed from each other to declare the blessed Jesus, and they assembled together, greeted each other, and said: [9] “Amen.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 86

1.text: Jesus then became visible, and said: “Peace be with you, and glory to those [who are faithful] in my name. Rise and go. Gladness will be yours, as well as grace with power.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 87

1.text: “Fear not. [I] will be with you continually.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 88

1.text: The apostles then departed [from each other as] they were sent out to preach, and] they went with the power of Jesus, with peace.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 89

1.text: [The] Letterof Peterto Philip
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 90

1.text: Notes
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 91

1.text: [1] “Verily,” or “yea,” not “yes,” given that here aeio (CT aio) is a liturgical interjection.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 92

1.text: [2] “You,” literally, “him.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 93

1.text: [3] “Your,” literally, “his.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 94

1.text: [4] “Small,” alluding to being human in contrast to being divine, which is great or large.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 95

1.text: [5] “Godless,” literally, “lawless.” See Nagel, 63.
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 96

1.text: [6] “Greeted,” (here and in CT) literally “kissed.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 97

1.text: [7] “Messages.” Nagel plausibly argues the Greek Vorlage referred to the four cardinal points. The Coptic scribe has played off the traditional associations between the four cardinal points and the four canonical gospels, which he here calls “speeches” (not four individual “words”) or “messages.”
1.label: Codex Tchacos · 98
